title: Optical Overlay Metrology - Overlay Shift Detection on Zeta-388
subtitle: Final Inspection Quality Validation for 45nm Node Manufacturing
author: James Rodriguez

sections.1_OBJECTIVE:
This test case validates the capability of the Zeta-388 system to detect and classify Overlay Shift defects during final inspection inspection at the 45nm technology node. The test is conducted at Hsinchu Fab 12 to ensure manufacturing quality standards are met for 300mm wafer production.

The primary objective is to verify that the inspection system meets the required detection sensitivity and classification accuracy for Overlay Shift defects that are critical to yield at the 45nm node. This test case is part of the ongoing qualification program for the Zeta-388 platform.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Product Line: Zeta-388
- Inspection Type: Optical Overlay Metrology
- Target Defect: Overlay Shift
- Process Step: Final Inspection
- Wafer Size: 300mm
- Technology Node: 45nm
- Fab Location: Hsinchu Fab 12

This test case applies to all Zeta-388 systems deployed at Hsinchu Fab 12 for final inspection monitoring in the 45nm manufacturing line. Results from this test are used to establish baseline performance metrics and to qualify new recipe configurations.
sections.3_TEST_CONFIGURATION:
System: Zeta-388
Software Version: v14.3.396
Recipe: OPTICAL_OVERLAY_METROLOGY_45nm_FINAL INSPECTION
Illumination Mode: Darkfield
Scan Speed: Low (147 mm/s)
Pixel Size: 0.1μm
Edge Exclusion: 2mm
Sampling Plan: Full wafer sampling
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Power on the Zeta-388 system and allow 30-minute warm-up period.
2. Load the calibration wafer and run the standard calibration routine.
3. Verify calibration results are within specification (±2% tolerance).
4. Load the test wafer onto the stage using the automated handler.
5. Select the 'Optical Overlay Metrology' recipe from the recipe library.
6. Configure detection sensitivity to target Overlay Shift defects.
7. Set scan parameters: full wafer scan with edge exclusion of 3mm.
8. Initiate the inspection run and monitor real-time defect map.
9. Upon completion, review the defect density map and classification results.
10. Export results to the factory automation system (SECS/GEM interface).
11. Compare results against the golden reference baseline.
12. Document any anomalies and generate the summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defect detection sensitivity must meet 45nm node requirements
- False positive rate shall not exceed 5% of total detected events
- Scan throughput must be ≥ 93 wafers per hour
- Classification accuracy shall be ≥ 99% for known defect types
- Repeatability (3-sigma) shall be within ±2.6% for Optical Overlay Metrology
- System uptime during test shall be ≥ 98%
- All results must be traceable through the MES integration
- Measurement correlation with reference tool shall be ≥ 0.95 R²
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Test Execution Date: 2024-02-10
Wafers Tested: 46
Total Defects Found: 2708
Defect Density: 383.1 defects/cm²
Nuisance Rate: 7.0%
Capture Rate: 96.9%
Test Duration: 265 minutes
System Uptime: 99.9%

Result Classification: PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Zeta-388 demonstrated excellent performance in detecting Overlay Shift at the 45nm node.

b) The capture rate exceeded the minimum threshold, confirming system readiness.

c) Nuisance rate exceeds the target threshold; recipe tuning is recommended.

d) Cross-correlation with the reference SEM confirmed classification accuracy.

e) The defect review station correlation was within specification.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS: No corrective actions required. Test passed all acceptance criteria.
